title: Replace the Correlated Subquery
statement: The `customers` table has columns id, name. The `orders` table has columns id, customer_id, amount. A teammate wrote this slow query to get each customer's order count: `SELECT c.id, c.name, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.id) AS order_count FROM customers c ORDER BY c.id;` - it runs one subquery per customer row. Write a more efficient query using a JOIN and GROUP BY that returns the exact same rows: `id, name, order_count` for every customer (including customers with zero orders), ordered by id.
starter_code:
SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(o.id) AS order_count
FROM customers c
-- TODO: join to orders so customers with zero orders are still included, then GROUP BY
ORDER BY c.id;
hints: A plain INNER JOIN would drop customers with no orders - use a LEFT JOIN instead
COUNT(o.id) counts only matched order rows, so a customer with no matches correctly counts as 0
GROUP BY c.id, c.name to collapse the joined rows back to one row per customer
